name: Namibia
tagline: Where the desert meets the wild
summary: The oldest desert on earth running into the Atlantic — Sossusvlei's dunes, the Skeleton Coast, Etosha's waterholes and Damaraland's desert elephant, across a country with almost nobody in it.

entries.caption: Where the Desert Meets the Wild
entries.description: The oldest desert on earth running straight into the Atlantic, and almost nobody on it.
entries.subject: red dunes at Sossusvlei with long morning shadows

entries.caption: The Namib
entries.description: Fifty-five million years old, and dunes at Sossusvlei three hundred metres high.
entries.subject: the dune field of the Namib at first light

entries.caption: Desert-Adapted Wildlife
entries.description: Elephant and rhino that walk sixty kilometres between water, and lion that hunt seals.
entries.subject: a desert-adapted elephant in a dry riverbed

entries.caption: Etosha
entries.description: Game that comes to you: in the dry season everything in the park is at one of the waterholes.
entries.subject: elephants and zebra at an Etosha waterhole

entries.caption: The Brandberg and the Escarpment
entries.description: The Brandberg is 2,573 metres and holds the White Lady, one of Africa's known rock paintings.
entries.subject: the granite mass of the Brandberg above the plain

entries.caption: Epupa
entries.description: The Kunene drops through a gorge on the Angolan border, with baobabs on the rim.
entries.subject: the Epupa falls on the Kunene river

entries.caption: The Kunene and the Zambezi
entries.description: Two permanent rivers, one on each border, and dry riverbeds for everything in between.
entries.subject: a dry riverbed cutting through Damaraland

entries.caption: The Skeleton Coast
entries.description: Fifteen hundred kilometres of Atlantic, fog, shipwrecks and seal colonies.
entries.subject: a shipwreck half-buried on the Skeleton Coast

entries.caption: The Caprivi Woodland
entries.description: No rainforest — the green is in the Zambezi region, riverine and full of elephant.
entries.subject: riverine woodland along the Zambezi in the Caprivi

entries.caption: Self-Drive Country
entries.description: The best self-drive country in Africa: gravel roads, long distances and nobody on them.
entries.subject: a gravel road running straight to the horizon

entries.caption: Eleven Peoples
entries.description: Owambo, Herero, Damara, Nama, San and more, and German still on half the street signs.
entries.subject: a Herero woman in traditional dress

entries.caption: The Himba
entries.description: The Himba of the Kunene, whose way of life is genuinely intact and should be visited carefully.
entries.subject: a Himba homestead in the Kunene region

entries.caption: Braai and Biltong
entries.description: Game meat over coals, biltong on every counter, and German bread that is actually German.
entries.subject: game meat grilling over coals at a Namibian braai

entries.caption: Windhoek Karnival and Maherero Day
entries.description: The Windhoek carnival in April, and Maherero Day at Okahandja in August.
entries.subject: a Maherero Day procession at Okahandja

entries.caption: Basketry and Ostrich Shell
entries.description: Kavango wood carving, San ostrich-eggshell beadwork, and Herero doll making.
entries.subject: San ostrich eggshell beads being strung

entries.caption: Twyfelfontein
entries.description: Two thousand rock engravings on one hillside, cut into sandstone six thousand years ago.
entries.subject: rock engravings on sandstone at Twyfelfontein

entries.caption: Kolmanskop and the Coast
entries.description: A diamond town the desert has taken back, and the German colonial coast at Lüderitz.
entries.subject: sand filling a room in the ghost town of Kolmanskop

entries.caption: Windhoek and Swakopmund
entries.description: Windhoek on the highveld, and Swakopmund where German architecture meets Atlantic fog.
entries.subject: the seafront and pier at Swakopmund in fog

entries.caption: Colonial and Desert Vernacular
entries.description: German colonial in the towns, and camps built to disappear into the gravel plains.
entries.subject: a desert lodge built low into the gravel plain

entries.caption: The Long Road
entries.description: Fuel, biltong and a farm stall every two hundred kilometres, and that is the day.
entries.subject: a roadside farm stall on a Namibian highway

entries.caption: Easy and Safe to Drive
entries.description: Good roads, no malaria in most of it, and children who will remember the dunes.
entries.subject: a family climbing a dune at Sossusvlei

entries.caption: Dune, Quad, Balloon
entries.description: Climbing Big Daddy, quad biking at Swakopmund, and balloons over the Namib at dawn.
entries.subject: a balloon over the Namib at sunrise

entries.caption: Desert Camps
entries.description: Small camps in private concessions the size of counties, and almost no light pollution.
entries.subject: a desert camp lit under a full sky of stars

entries.caption: Conservancies
entries.description: Communal conservancies cover a fifth of the country and are why the black rhino survived.
entries.subject: a community game guard on patrol in a conservancy

entries.caption: The Cleanest Light in Africa
entries.description: Dry air, no haze, and one of the darkest night skies measured anywhere.
entries.subject: the Milky Way over a Namibian desert landscape

entries.caption: The Kunene
entries.description: The far north-west: Epupa, the Himba, and roads that need two vehicles.
entries.subject: a track through the mountains of the Kunene region

entries.caption: Space, and the Silence in It
entries.description: Two and a half million people in a country twice the size of Germany.
entries.subject: an empty gravel plain stretching to distant mountains
